sourceEvidence.claim: Gram stain — definition (first-line; thick retains violet, thin turns red/pink)
sourceEvidence.quote:
First-line lab test in bacterial identification. Bacteria with thick peptidoglycan layer retain crystal
violet dye (gram ⊕); bacteria with thin peptidoglycan layer turn red or pink (gram ⊝) with
counterstain.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Poor-stainer block (full physical order, incl. FA mnemonic for verification only)
sourceEvidence.quote:
These bugs do not Gram stain well (These Little Microbes May Unfortunately Lack Real Color
But Are Everywhere):
Treponema, Leptospira
Too thin to be visualized
Mycobacteria
Cell wall has high lipid content
Mycoplasma, Ureaplasma
No cell wall
Legionella, Rickettsia, Chlamydia, Bartonella,
Anaplasma, Ehrlichia
Primarily intracellular; also, Chlamydia lack
classic peptidoglycan because of ↓ muramic
acid
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the stains table; the USMLE question attack structure is a KYP design.
kypExtensions.location: usmle section (patterns, traps, pivots, miniCase) + recall/rapidReview

kypExtensions.summary: The unified model: every stain reads one structure (wall thickness for gram; mycolic-acid wall for acid-fast; capsule for ink/mucicarmine; polysaccharides for PAS; antibody targets for FA) and the four poor-stainer modes are four anatomies that break the gram readout — with the workaround algorithm ('gram failed → pick the stain that reads the structure you suspect'), the stain-failure vs culture-failure distinction, and the extension notes (darkfield/serology for the spirochetes; cold agglutinins/Eaton agar for Mycoplasma) labeled as extensions.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source lists stains and organisms without the structure→readout model or the failure-mode taxonomy; these integrations are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanism caption + callout + patterns + mnemonics + miniCase
